subject: ggplot2: bar plot looked great until I sorted a column

messages.author: 3ecebeec78f948e2
messages.subject: ggplot2: bar plot looked great until I sorted a column
parts:
Hello! 

I'm a new ggplot user and am just stumbling through the darkness. I've managed to almost make the bar chart I want, but I decided to go wild and sort one value by size but that screwed things up. So let me see if I can walk you through what I have and what I want:

Code that almost works: 
ggplot(data, aes(y=average, x=Year, fill=Pass.Fail))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity", color="black", position="dodge")




Problem with above graph: I want the sections of each bar organized from largest at the bottom to smallest section at the top. 


What I did: I organized the column of those values numerically and figured either it would produce what I want (even if it's backwards) or change nothing at all. Insead, the sections of each bar disappeared entirely. 


Using "order" to organize that column of data:

 ordereddata<-data[order(data$average),]



New Code:

 ggplot(ordereddata, aes(y=average, x=Year, fill=Pass.Fail))+

   geom_bar(stat="identity", color="black", position="dodge") 



At this point I don't even know if the final version is what I want but I'm determined to figure out where I went wrong and how to make this work. Any help would be greatly appreciated!


Thank you, 


Elizabeth

messages.author: 7a2af6319a63135a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: ggplot2: bar plot looked great until I sorted a column
parts:
Hi Elizabeth,

I think the issue is actually arising from using position = “dodge”. When you change to “dodge”, your bars are actually no longer stacked. Look at your data- for the year 2010, what is the highest value for “average”? If you total up the “average” values for 2010 Fails, will it be 200 or far more? I think your bars are actually getting layered one in front of the other within each year+pass.fail category, rather than stacked on top of each other.

If you do position = “stacked”, should stack correctly, but then Pass.Fail will be stacked on top of each other. One way around that is to use x = pass.fail , position = “stacked”, and facet.grid(~year) to put years side by side, with separate stacked bars for pass and fail.

I played with some dummy data to make these plots, take a look and see if they work for you:

library(tidyverse)

set.seed(51)
d <- tibble(year = rep(2012:2015, 5), average = sample(10:70, 20), 
            pass_fail = sample(c("fail", "pass"), 20, replace = T))

# how tall should each bar be if we stack by year+pass_fail combination?
d %>% 
  group_by(year, pass_fail)%>% 
  summarise(sum(average))

# arrange data by descending average, and then plot with position = "dodge"
d %>% 
  arrange(desc(average)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = average, fill = pass_fail, group = pass_fail)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", color = "black")
# take a look at 2012 fail the bar is like 69 tall, but according to our summary table it should be 195. the bars are getting placed one in front of the other, not stacked

# this should get the plot we want
d %>% 
  arrange(desc(average)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = pass_fail, y = average, fill = pass_fail, group = pass_fail)) +
  geom_col(color = "black") +
  facet_grid(~year)


Michael Culshaw-Maurer
Grad Group in Ecology
Rosenheim/Schreiber Labs
Briggs 320
